turns.prompt_text: I am trying to shuffle a deck of cards by splitting it in half and then doing the alternate pattern after I flip them. Now that I have them in a exact pattern, I want to do the second part where I bend all the cards heavily and hold the tops with my thumbs so that they make a loud sound as the Cascade I know it damages the cars by bending them but I've never been able to do it
turns.response_html:
That loud, satisfying cascade is called the "Bridge Finish." First, to gently correct a common myth: this move actually prevents long-term damage to the cards! When you riffle the deck, you bend the cards downward. The bridge bends them back upward, neutralizing the curve and keeping the deck flat. Casinos use it specifically to extend the life of their decks.

The reason most people fail the cascade is that they try to push the cards down with their thumbs. The entire trick actually happens underneath the deck with your fingers.

Your dominant left hand might naturally try to pull away faster or release pressure sooner during the final step—focus on letting both hands relax and drift apart at the exact same speed to keep the cascade perfectly even.
